faqs: Which Burj Khalifa ticket should I choose?

For most first-time visitors, Silver (levels 124 and 125) gives the classic view at the lowest price. Choose Prime Time for sunset, Gold for a quieter hosted deck on level 148, or Platinum for the highest lounge on levels 152–154.

What is the difference between Prime and Non-Prime tickets?

Prime Time tickets are for the busiest slots, mainly the hours around sunset, and cost more. Non-Prime covers the rest of the day. The view and levels are the same; only the entry time and price differ. Our team confirms the exact slot times for your date.
What is the dress code?

There is no formal dress code, but modest, comfortable clothing is expected, as across The Dubai Mall. Covering shoulders and knees is a safe choice. Wear comfortable shoes and bring a light layer for the outdoor terrace, which can be windy.
What are the conditions for children?
Children aged 0–3 enter free but still need a ticket at check-in. Children must stay with an adult at all times. Strollers are not allowed on the decks and must be left in the luggage room.
How long does the visit take?
Allow 1.5 to 2 hours in total. That includes check-in, the exhibition walk, the lift and around 40 minutes on the decks. Fast Track tickets can cut this to about 1 hour.
How do I find the check-in desk?

The At the Top entrance is on the lower ground (LG) level of The Dubai Mall. From the metro link bridge or any car park, follow the signs for At the Top / Burj Khalifa. Arrive 20–30 minutes before your slot.
Do I need to print my ticket?
No. Show the mobile ticket on your phone with a valid photo ID. Each guest needs their own QR code, so keep all tickets ready if you booked for a group.
What documents are required for entry?
Bring a valid photo ID such as a passport, Emirates ID or driving licence. A digital copy is usually accepted.
What should I do if I am late?

Contact us right away on +971 50 559 9243 or WhatsApp. Entry depends on your time slot, and late arrivals may be refused or moved to the next available slot at the venue's discretion. Tickets are usually non-refundable once the slot has passed.
May I bring my own food and drinks?
No. Outside food and drinks are not allowed on the observation decks. You can eat before or after your visit in The Dubai Mall, or choose a Burj Club Rooftop option.
Can I cancel or change my Burj Khalifa ticket?

At the Top general admission tickets are usually final once issued and cannot be refunded or changed. Our team confirms the policy for your chosen option on WhatsApp before you pay, so check it then and contact us if your plans change.
What is the best time to visit Burj Khalifa?

About 30 minutes before sunset gives daylight, golden hour and city lights in one visit, but it is the busiest and dearest slot. Early morning and late evening are quieter and cheaper. Winter (November to March) usually has the clearest air.
How do I get to Burj Khalifa by metro?
Take the Red Line to Burj Khalifa/Dubai Mall station, then follow the air-conditioned link bridge into The Dubai Mall. The walk to the At the Top entrance takes about 10–15 minutes.
Is Burj Khalifa At the Top wheelchair accessible?

Yes. The entrance, lifts and observation decks are wheelchair accessible, and staff can help visitors with extra needs. Strollers are not allowed on the decks, so plan to leave them in the luggage room.

overview: Louvre Abu Dhabi sits on the water in the Saadiyat Cultural District and opened in November 2017. It calls itself a universal museum: rather than splitting art by country, its galleries follow a timeline, so you walk from early civilisations through to modern and contemporary work and see how cultures influenced each other. Its own collection is shown alongside loans from French museums such as the Musée du Louvre, the Musée d'Orsay and the Centre Pompidou.

The building, designed by Jean Nouvel, is part of the visit. A wide dome of interlaced stars covers the open plaza, and sunlight passing through it falls on the floor and water below in moving spots of light that the museum calls the "rain of light". The dome area, cafés and restaurants stay open until midnight, after the galleries close.

The ticket covers the permanent galleries, the temporary exhibitions and the Children's Museum, and you can use the museum's free app to learn more about the works as you go. KWIKAR sells the open-dated ticket, so you do not need to fix the day in advance. Our team checks your request and confirms the final price before you pay. overview: The Abu Dhabi Grand Prix is the final round of the 2026 Formula 1 season. It runs over four days from Thursday 3 to Sunday 6 December at Yas Marina Circuit. Thursday is the opening fan day, practice runs on Friday, qualifying on Saturday and the race on Sunday, with Formula 2 and other support races around the main sessions. The circuit sits on Yas Island next to Ferrari World, Yas Marina and the W Abu Dhabi – Yas Island hotel.

Where you sit decides what you see. The North Straight, West Straight, West and North Grandstands face the longest straight and the braking zones into Turns 5–7, where most overtaking happens. The Main Grandstand looks over the grid, pit stops, finish line and podium. The South Grandstand faces Marsa Corner (Turn 9) and the marina. Abu Dhabi Hill is open grass with no reserved seats, and the Club and hospitality options add air-conditioned lounges, food and drinks.

Each night the Yasalam After-Race Concerts take place at Etihad Park, and general admission is included with every race ticket for that day. The 4-day passes also include one day at a participating Abu Dhabi attraction, such as a Yas Island theme park like Ferrari World or teamLab Phenomena Abu Dhabi. Not sure which park to pick? visitor_info: Getting there

Yas Marina Circuit is on Yas Island, between Abu Dhabi city and Dubai. On site, free circuit shuttle buses link the grandstands, you can walk in from Yas Marina via the North Oasis, and taxis drop off at Etihad Park. From Dubai or Abu Dhabi Airport, a private transfer or a car to Yas Island from Dubai Airport takes you close to the gates; the organisers publish the 2026 transport and parking plan nearer the race.
Your ticket

Tickets are digital and open only in the official Abu Dhabi GP app; screenshots and printouts are not accepted. The QR code appears in the app closer to the event. Our team sends your ticket details at least 3 days before the event.
Bags and banned items

Bags are searched at the gates. Not allowed: your own food and drinks (baby food and medical diets with a doctor's letter are fine), alcohol, bottles and cans (refillable water containers are allowed), umbrellas bought outside, chairs, cooler boxes, large backpacks, video cameras and GoPros, camera lenses over 30 cm, drones, scooters, air horns and flags on poles over 1 metre.
The concerts

Concert gates at Etihad Park open at 6pm, and general admission is first come, first served. The organisers list Lewis Capaldi on Thursday, Jennifer Lopez with Alex Warren on Friday, Imagine Dragons on Saturday and The Chainsmokers with The Script on Sunday; line-ups can change, so check the official site before you go.
Children and age limits

Children under 2 do not need a ticket; everyone aged 2 and over needs their own pass, and our options have no separate child rate. Some hospitality areas only admit guests over 12 or over 21, alcohol is served only to over-21s with photo ID, and the After-Party is 21+. Send the ages in your group and our team confirms which options suit you.
What to bring

December days on Yas Island are usually warm and evenings cooler, so bring sunscreen, a hat, a light layer for the night and a refillable water bottle. Ear protection is a good idea for children and anyone sensitive to noise.
